stories.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
stories.titleZh: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
stories.summaryZhShort: This may be a hot take, but I strongly believe that all code generated by AI should be Open Source. And here's why.First of all, AI models were trained on a massive corpus of Open Source code written since RMS announced...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: This may be a hot take, but I strongly believe that all code generated by AI should be Open Source. And here's why.First of all, AI models were trained on a massive corpus of Open Source code written since RMS announced the GNU Project and the Free Software Movement. That code was simply scraped from the internet and used without permission or proper attribution. The models were also trained on Stack Overflow and Stack Exchange sister projects, which are released under Creative Commons licenses that legally require attribution. Turning this collective knowledge into proprietary, closed-source code feels like license laundering.The second reason is legal: purely AI-generated code is not written by a human, meaning it should not be copyrightable. The foundation for this principle in the US goes back to the famous Monkey Selfie dispute, which established that non-humans cannot hold copyrights. A precedent later cited by the U.S. Copyright Office regarding AI. Following the same logic, Wikimedia Commons requires all purely AI-generated images to be tagged as Public Domain.However, copyright laws differ across the globe. For instance, countries like the UK grant limited copyright protection to computer-generated works. To make things fair across all jurisdictions, and to honor the open ecosystem that made AI possible, developers and companies should explicitly release AI-generated code under Open Source licenses or dedicate it to the public domain using the Creative Commons Zero (CC0) license.Of course, code is not always 100% manual or 100% automated. However, developers more and more rely on AI without even reviewing the generated output, let alone modifying it to fit their specific needs. Code like this, where humans put little effort, except writing prompts, should definitely be Open Source.If you find this article interesting you may want to follow me on Twitter: @jcubic and on LinkedIn.See hacker news for discussion

stories.title: Many of Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday “deals” offered no savings
stories.titleZh: Many of Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday “deals” offered no savings
stories.summaryZhShort: November 16, 2026 Amazon’s Decoy Deals: Groundwork Investigation Reveals Nearly 1 in 3 Black Friday and Cyber Monday “Deals” Advertised by Amazon Offered No Savings to Shoppers, Nearly 1 in 10 Were Actually More...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: November 16, 2026

Amazon’s Decoy Deals: Groundwork Investigation Reveals Nearly 1 in 3 Black Friday and Cyber Monday “Deals” Advertised by Amazon Offered No Savings to Shoppers, Nearly 1 in 10 Were Actually More Expensive A blockbuster new investigation from Groundwork Collaborative exposes how Amazon shoppers may be getting hosed during the retail giant’s much-touted Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale events. The report, Deal or Decoy? Amazon’s Deceptive Discounts, examines products the retailer showcased as some the “best” discounts of the year to shoppers hunting for bargains during these sale events. A closer look at hundreds of these “deals” finds that Amazon frequently offered shoppers the same price, or in some cases a higher price, during recent holiday sale events than they could have paid just weeks earlier. The report’s authors, Breyon Williams, Elizabeth Pancotti, and Lindsay Owens, find that nearly 1 in 3 of these Amazon “deals” offered no real savings – the exact same products were sold for the same price or less in the month before the sale. During Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales in the past two years, prices for nearly 1 in 10 products advertised as “deals” were higher than what customers could have paid for the products in the month leading up to the sales. Groundwork’s analysis examined the prices of more than 350 products included on Amazon’s own deal pages for the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale events in 2024 and 2025. These pages promote these deals as some of the “best” deals available. Amazon’s Black Friday 2025 deals page says, “With so many deals to explore, we’ve handpicked some of the best ones you’ll find.” Groundwork Collaborative President and CEO and report co-author Lindsay Owens, shared the following reaction: “Millions of Americans wait all year for Black Friday and Cyber Monday to score the biggest bargains on stocking stuffers and household staples. Shoppers trust that the deals advertised to them deliver real savings because Amazon promotes them that way. But it turns out that these major sales aren’t all they’re cracked up to be. Instead, our investigation reveals that shoppers who wait for these major sale events may be playing rip-off roulette. “Amazon dominates online shopping, and families count on its sale events to stretch their dollars. With the holiday shopping season upon us and prices continuing to rise, shoppers deserve to know they can trust every deal Amazon promises them. If Amazon can’t deliver that basic promise, lawmakers should hold them accountable.” Owens is the author of the recent book Gouged: The End of a Fair Price—And What That Means for Your Wallet, which exposes how corporations are sophisticated pricing schemes to overcharge consumers.

stories.title: Windows 11 is collecting data on which coding agents and developer tools you use
stories.titleZh: Windows 11 is collecting data on which coding agents and developer tools you use
stories.summaryZhShort: Reverse engineering Windows 11's MissionControlAggregator reveals coding-agent and developer-tool usage bits in a diagnostic ETW report. I recently asked AI to help me look through the latest Windows binaries for...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 5 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: Reverse engineering Windows 11's MissionControlAggregator reveals coding-agent and developer-tool usage bits in a diagnostic ETW report. I recently asked AI to help me look through the latest Windows binaries for undocumented features and functionality. Among the leads it turned up, one list immediately caught my attention: coding agents such as codex.exe, claude.exe, copilot.exe, and cursor.exe, alongside familiar developer tools such as python.exe, dotnet.exe, gcc.exe, and code.exe. Why would a Windows system DLL need a list of coding agents and developer tools? The names were in MissionControlAggregator.dll. I asked the agent to follow the references and dig into what the DLL actually does. That led from a handful of string comparisons to a running Windows component that records which coding agents and developer tools have been used, saves that information locally, and reports it to Windows Diagnostics. And unless you have opted out of the “optional” diagnostic data (which is enabled by default), the data is uploaded to Microsoft. I shared the initial finding on X. This post includes more details about the investigation behind it. Following the names Opening the DLL in Binary Ninja made the first lead easy to see. These were explicit executable names embedded in a Windows component:

Following the references showed that the names were used in comparisons. There are four CLI-agent slots checking copilot.exe, claude.exe, codex.exe, and agy.exe, with extensionless equivalents on the WSL route. Five desktop-agent slots check github.exe, claude.exe, codex.exe, cursor.exe, and antigravity.exe. Here is one of the comparisons against codex.exe:

stories.title: Lovable apps expose passport details and more than 200K private messages
stories.titleZh: Lovable apps expose passport details and more than 200K private messages
stories.summaryZhShort: Lovable: Many Apps Built on the Platform Expose Sensitive DataAI makes it easier to build your own web applications, but handling sensitive data still requires special care. We examined 159,041 Lovable projects and found...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: Lovable: Many Apps Built on the Platform Expose Sensitive DataAI makes it easier to build your own web applications, but handling sensitive data still requires special care. We examined 159,041 Lovable projects and found many cases where personal and confidential information was accessible without logging in.Diesen Artikel auf Deutsch lesenAbout LovableLovable is a Swedish AI startup founded in Stockholm in 2023 by Anton Osika and Fabian Hedin. The platform turns plain-language descriptions into web applications and is designed to be accessible even to people with little or no programming experience.Lovable grew out of Osika’s open-source project “GPT Engineer”, released in 2023. The project evolved into the GPT Engineer App before being renamed Lovable in late 2024 and launching publicly that November.Visit the Lovable websiteThe PromiseLovable can build impressively sophisticated web projects with AI, from static websites to full applications with user management and database connections. But as soon as an application handles confidential information, one question becomes crucial: Is that data protected against unauthorized access?In its marketing, Lovable repeatedly emphasizes that no technical knowledge is needed to build projects. This can give the impression that the platform takes care of security too. Yet Lovable’s Terms & Conditions place responsibility for applications and data handling on the customers themselves.That leaves a troubling gap between the promise of an easy-to-use, all-in-one service and the responsibilities customers are expected to take on.Against this backdrop, we investigated how well sensitive data in Lovable applications is protected, in collaboration with Handelsblatt. Lina Knees reported on the findings on November 2, 2026 (in German).Research QuestionWe wanted to find out whether sensitive data in Lovable applications was accessible without logging in. We looked separately at data sent when a website first loaded and additional content we checked by making further read-only requests with the same API key.The result: We found many clear examples of sensitive data left unprotected.MethodologyWe focused on the database service Supabase. Its integration is relatively easy to analyze, and we believe it is the most widely used database service among Lovable projects. Lovable’s own database features, introduced in late 2025, are still less widely used. Similar misconfigurations may occur there too, but we did not examine them in this analysis.Using datasets from the open web archive Common Crawl, we identified and analyzed 159,041 Lovable projects from December 2025 to September 2026. Of these, 34,545 used Supabase.24,664 websites sent database records from Supabase as soon as they loaded, without requiring a login or any other interaction. That alone is not a security issue: the data may be intended for public display. But by making additional read-only requests, we were able to retrieve more database content. We found records containing email addresses in 10,560 tables across 7,403 of the 24,664 websites (30%).LimitationsEmail addresses can help identify records containing personal data, but they may also be public contact addresses or test data. At the same time, this approach misses personal records that contain no email address. These effects partly offset one another, though we could not establish to what extent. The 30% figure should therefore not be read as a confirmed data leak rate. It applies only to the 24,664 websites we examined more closely. Our sample, drawn from Common Crawl, is also not representative of all Lovable applications.We retrieved only parts of the datasets rather than downloading them in full. The figures below reflect the records we actually downloaded; the affected datasets may contain more. We are not publishing details of how to access them, as doing so could make further access easier.Data LeaksWe found many serious cases of exposed data, including:A German lifestyle forum exposed more than 80,000 profiles containing full names, email addresses, dates of birth, and gender information. More than 200,000 chat messages were also accessible.Several event organizers and restaurants exposed tens of thousands of records relating to ticket and food sales, with no login required. The records we inspected included email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses, payment information, and ticket codes.A property management company exposed AI-generated summaries of internal emails containing sensitive information about tenants, property owners, and business partners.In a particularly serious case, a service provider exposed more than 1,000 records containing identity document details, including passport numbers, expiration dates, and nationalities. These highly sensitive identity details could be used for identity theft.Other accessible content included tens of thousands of contracts, invoices, personal photo albums, and internal WhatsApp communications.We also found numerous newsletter subscriptions, waiting lists, and contact and support inquiries. In one case, 280,000 emails sent to a provider’s customers were accessible.Depending on what it contains, exposed data like this could be used for phishing, ticket fraud, or identity theft. We could not establish whether any of it had been misused.Handelsblatt contacted Lovable with the findings of our investigation.ImplicationsOur analysis shows that many Lovable applications leave even highly sensitive data unprotected, with potentially serious consequences for the people affected.Access control mistakes can happen in any application, whether written by people or built with AI. With Lovable, database integrations follow recurring patterns, making it easier for attackers to look for similar misconfigurations across many applications. An approach that works against one app may then work against others with little extra effort. Users without a technical background also face a harder task spotting and preventing these flaws.An easy-to-use development platform does not remove the need for an expert review of access permissions before an application handles confidential data.Automated checks are no substitute for a professional security assessment.Before an application handles real customer or business data, its access permissions, interfaces, and separation between user accounts should be reviewed. These checks should be repeated after significant changes. If the necessary expertise is not available in-house, bring in qualified support.If you would like help securing your application, please get in touch.Note: This research report presents a more recent analysis and updated figures compared with the Handelsblatt article published on November 2, 2026.Get in touch for an informal conversation. We'll look at your current situation and work with you to find the right solutions.Contact an expert

stories.title: What's Next for Nvidia?
stories.titleZh: What's Next for Nvidia?
stories.summaryZhShort: Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang had resigned 33 years after he co-founded the company. What happens to a company when a visionary CEO is gone? Most often innovation dies and the company coasts for years on...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 8 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang had resigned 33 years after he co-founded the company. What happens to a company when a visionary CEO is gone? Most often innovation dies and the company coasts for years on momentum and its brand. Rarely does it regain its former glory. That’s the danger facing Nvidia. Here’s what their board should be considering. Here’s why.

Jensen Huang reinvented Nvidia three times. In 2006 he launched CUDA, turning a graphics chip for PC gamers into a general-purpose computing platform – and funded it for years ahead of any revenue. In 2012, when researchers used Nvidia chips to win the ImageNet contest, he pointed the company to deep learning. In 2020, with the acquisition of Mellanox, Nvidia went from selling boards with GPUs to selling integrated racks that power AI datacenters. These were not just product transitions, but radical business model transitions; new channels, new customers and new markets. Nvidia pivoted from a vendor of graphics boards, to a software platform, and then to systems company. It’s hard to imagine a CEO focused on executing an existing business model funding CUDA through those years.

stories.summaryZhShort: Diesem Problem waren wir alle ausgesetzt: Am Freitag gab es eine Störung, die den US-Softwarekonzern Microsoft lahmgelegt hat. Unter anderem das E-Mail-Programm Outlook. Betroffen war auch das Phantasialand. Durch die...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: Diesem Problem waren wir alle ausgesetzt: Am Freitag gab es eine Störung, die den US-Softwarekonzern Microsoft lahmgelegt hat. Unter anderem das E-Mail-Programm Outlook. Betroffen war auch das Phantasialand. Durch die Störung kamen keine Mails an, wie das Unternehmen dem WDR am Samstag mitteilte. So bekam niemand mit, dass das Wartungssicherheitssystem der Saunalandschaft längst per Mail Alarm geschlagen hat. Denn das automatischen Dosiersystem hatte zu viel Chlor in den Pool gepumpt. Reizungen der Atemwege Dadurch wurden Gäste im Hotel Ling Bao des Phantasialands in Brühl verletzt. Sie haben über gesundheitliche Probleme geklagt, nachdem sie den Pool besucht hatten. Der wurde zeitweise gesperrt, konnte inzwischen aber wieder freigegeben werden, wie die Feuerwehr am Samstag dem WDR mitteilte. Wegen der Beschwerden der Hotel-Besucher wurden Rettungskräfte und die Feuerwehr gerufen. 13 Gäste klagten über Reizungen der Atemwege, letztlich stieg die Zahl der Betroffenen auf insgesamt 15. Überhöhter Chlorgehalt: Eine Person bleibt im Krankenhaus Zunächst hieß es, dass fünf Gäste ins Krankenhaus gebracht wurden, später wurde die Zahl auf vier korrigiert, eine Person davon blieb wegen einer mittelschweren Verletzung zur Beobachtung im Krankenhaus. Im Hotel ergaben Tests der Einsatzkräfte einen Defekt des automatischen Dosiersystems für den Pool. Dies hatte zu einem deutlich überhöhten Chlorgehalt geführt. Das Wasser wurde daher ausgetauscht. Betreiber der Mauritius-Therme wird hellhörig Die Nachricht über den Chlorunfall im Hotel im Phantasialand hat auch Max Wiesen, den Betreiber von "Mauritius Hotel und Therme", hellhörig werden lassen.
"Da denkt man natürlich immer selber: Oh je, kann uns das auch passieren?" Max Wiesen, Betreiber von "Mauritius Hotel und Therme"

summaryZh: tl;drour 3rd release, a full color 31.5" ePaper display in a handmade wooden frame, is now available for pre-order. watch the short film:the 1st batch is just ~470 units and i intend to ship at least a few by the end of 2026. most deliveries will happen early 2027. see logistics for more details or pre-order here.backgroundin 2013 i founded ArtSpot. our vision was to give New Yorkers a bit of joy by exposing them to local art. we did this through informal agreements with dozens of cafes, small galleries, and restaurants. "let us curate art on your walls, get paid if someone buys it."and it worked. sort of. finding artists was easy, building the platform was easy. getting permission from venues was slow but straightforward. the problem was nobody actually bought the art. i remember the admin email notification that first time a piece was sold. it was a small painting of Janelle Monáe. the buyer was my friend, a gift to me. here it is, still in my possession.

anyway ArtSpot failed. five years later i paid back my investors (+ 13% interest). but the vision never went away. i love making and consuming art.opinionated platformi probably say "the most popular feature request since launch is ______" too often. after saying no (and yes) to so many requests, it's tough to keep count.but with certainty, one of our strongest convictions was about color. TRMNL is not a television. it is not a clock. we avoid trying to do too much.then grayscale happened. photos look great. art is possible. community member Clark debuted Jaws (yes the movie), 1 frame at a time.

stories.summaryZhShort: 最近刚入手了一个掌阅 Ocean6 Pro，老的 kindle 用了 11 年了，新老交接。 Kindle 是 Paperwhite （第七代），其他的功能一切正常，就是电池不太耐用了，充电变得频繁了一些。这个 Kindle 陪我看完了阿婆的所有小说（波洛和马普尔小姐系列）

summaryZh: 最近刚入手了一个掌阅 Ocean6 Pro，老的 kindle 用了 11 年了，新老交接。

stories.summaryZhShort: 我今天短信收到了很多快递信息，然后我打开了 Siri，问它能不能查一下短信，把快递信息给我找出来。它一直说：“你没有新信息，你没有新信息。”
